target_customer: Individuals paying out of pocket for in-person therapy, and their therapists
problem: Therapy lacks data and continuity between sessions, so progress is hard to track.
business_model: Flat rate per session in-person therapy paired with a private app (about 165 USD per session, no insurance, per a third-party summary)
product_category: Digital mental health, therapy plus app

founders.name: Ti Zhao
founders.background_notes: YC bio says they focus on public health and the effect of the built environment on health

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile check in app and analytics layered on a services business.

defensibility.rationale: Therapist relationships and data were small; the app was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Modern Health, a digital mental health benefits company, acquired Kip in February 2021 and the CEO joined its product team.

market_need_then: Not independently sourced for 2016; Kip positioned itself as improving in-person therapy rather than replacing it.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; a different product also named Kip exists, so the name was confusable.

outcome_analysis: Kip combined in-person therapy with a data tracking app, went through YC in Winter 2016 and was acquired by Modern Health on 1 February 2021, with the CEO joining that company's product team. No funding rounds could be verified, so the scale and quality of the exit are unclear. It looks like a small team sale rather than a large venture outcome, but that is not stated by any source.
notes: YC page lists only Ti Zhao; press names Erin Frey as co-founder and CEO in a 2017 YC post, but she is not listed on the YC page, so omitted from founders. CB Insights lists 120K over 4 rounds with placeholder amounts and Healthcare Discovery found no Form D; unverified, not recorded. The hellokip.com fetch returned a 503. Competitor search returned only later era lists, so the list is empty.
